system.name: TreeVAE
system.one_liner: Generative hierarchical clustering model with a learned tree-structured posterior over latent variables and specialised leaf decoders.

content.variant_note: a learned binary tree whose ten leaves each carry a framed 3x3 mosaic of CIFAR-10 images and a name pill; model-anatomy because the circles are the model's latent variables, though no network is drawn
content.argues: Without labels, TreeVAE discovers a tree on CIFAR-10 that separates animals from vehicles and groups similar classes under shared ancestors.
content.subject: The hierarchy learned on CIFAR-10: a binary tree of latent-variable circles with sample images assigned to each of ten leaves.

layout.arrangement_note: One wide binary tree drawn top-down on white: the root at top centre, ten leaves along the bottom, each with a short down arrow onto a 3x3 image mosaic and a rounded grey pill below; mosaics under deeper leaves hang lower so all arrows have the same length; animals and vehicles pills sit beside the first splits.

new_tags.name: tree-with-thumbnail-leaves
new_tags.what: a tree or hierarchy whose leaves each hold a framed thumbnail mosaic and a name pill

lessons.what_to_learn: Show a learned hierarchy by drawing the tree itself and hanging a framed mosaic of real samples under every leaf with a one-word pill, so the quality of the grouping can be judged from the pictures alone.
lessons.suits: Hierarchical clustering, taxonomy discovery or tree-structured latent models on image data, where the coherence of the leaves is the evidence.

evidence: An example of a tree learned by TreeVAE is depicted in Fig. 1.
In CIFAR-10, for example, the method divides the vehicles and animals into two different subtrees

summary: TreeVAE is a generative hierarchical clustering model that learns a tree-shaped posterior over latent variables and gives each leaf its own decoder. Figure 1 shows the tree it discovered on CIFAR-10, without using labels. A binary tree of open circles is drawn top-down; the first split gives an animals subtree with six leaves and a vehicles subtree with four. Each of the ten leaves points by a short arrow to a framed 3x3 mosaic of random images assigned to it and a grey pill names the class: horses, dogs, birds, cats, frogs, deers, trucks, cars, ships, planes. The drawing is black line work on white, with colour only in the photographs.
